title: Tight Time-Space Lower Bounds for Collision Finding and Element Distinctness under Label Symmetry
summary: How much memory is needed to retain the quantum speedup for collision finding? For a uniformly random function $f:[N]\to [N]$, the BHT algorithm finds a collision using $O(N^{1/3})$ queries and a quantumly accessible classical table containing $O(N^{1/3})$ input-output pairs, whereas a logarithmic-space Grover search uses $O(\sqrt N)$ queries. Determining the optimal query-space tradeoff between these extremes remains a major open problem.
